items.claim: The presence of a smartphone can reduce available cognitive capacity, especially for those who depend on their smartphones.
items.quote: Results from two experiments indicate that even when people are successful at maintaining sustained attention—as when avoiding the temptation to check their phones—the mere presence of these devices reduces available cognitive capacity.

items.claim: The presence of a smartphone reduces working memory capacity, but does not affect other cognitive functions like sustained attention.
items.quote: Working memory capacity was negatively impacted by the mere presence of a smartphone, while results for the remaining cognitive functions produced null summary effects.

items.claim: The mere presence of a smartphone can lead to lower cognitive performance in attention tasks.
items.quote: The results of the conducted experiment imply that the mere presence of a smartphone results in lower cognitive performance, which supports the hypothesis of the smartphone presence using limited cognitive resources.

check.causal: causal wording, but the cited study only shows an association

items.claim: The presence of a smartphone has no significant effect on cognitive outcomes overall.
items.quote: It was found that the mere presence of smartphone had no significant effect on cognitive outcomes (d = −0.02, SE = 0.02, 95% CI [−0.06, 0.01], p = .246).

items.claim: Emotion-related impulsivity traits can moderate the impact of smartphone presence on working memory.
items.quote: This study tested whether individual differences in emotion-related impulsivity traits (positive urgency and negative urgency) moderate the effect of smartphone availability on cognitive performance.

claims.verdict: Overall, the evidence suggests that the mere presence of a smartphone can reduce cognitive capacity, particularly affecting working memory, but findings are mixed and depend on individual differences.
claims.caveat: The studies show mixed results, with some indicating significant cognitive impacts while others find no effect, highlighting the need for further research to reconcile these differences.

explain.headline: Here's what's happening to your brain:
explain.body: Your phone's presence saps cognitive resources, particularly affecting working memory. This happens even if you're not using it.

matters.headline: Why should you care?
matters.body: This may be why you feel less focused when your phone is within sight, even if idle. Your cognitive performance can be subtly compromised.

example.headline: An Ordinary Moment:
example.body: Picture sitting at your desk with a smartphone nearby, open but idle. Your memory tasks may be getting harder without you realizing it.
